about: The evangelium of the formulary “10th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus addressed this parable to certain people who relied on themselves as though they were just, and held the rest in contempt: Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee and the second a publican. The Pharisee, standing, prayed these words within himself: O God, I give You thanks that I am not as the rest of mankind, robbers, unjust, adulterers, as this publican also is. I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of everything I possess. And the publican, standing far off, would not even raise his eyes toward heaven, but was beating his breast, saying: O God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.
